$comment: Every stable Criogen error code (design 0013 §2). Codes may be added, never renamed or removed before 1.0. Checked against the Rust sources, docs/errors.md and both SDKs by tests.

codes.description: A workflow node returned an error.
A Rust node panicked; the run failed instead of the process.
A node attempt took longer than its policy timeout.
A router function returned an error.
A router returned a label with no edge.
A node that must choose the next node did not.
A saved task memo entry does not have the shape the node asks for (or a value to save is not JSON); seen as the kind of a node_failed error.
Two nodes wrote the same state key in one step without a reducer.
The run reached its step limit.
The run reached its deadline, or the next retry would pass it.
The run was cancelled (a cancel token, an AbortSignal, a dropped stream, an interrupt from another process). In a tool message: a call that never got a result.
A value was not accepted: a state write a reducer cannot apply, a memory key, value, namespace or vector, a configuration value.
A resume or approval decision does not match what the run waits for.
A snapshot was made by a different workflow.
Saving the run's progress failed; details carry the storage code.
A model call failed after retries and fallbacks; details.model_error has the kind, and retryable follows it.

A tool failed with an error it did not handle (an exception, a panic). By default the model sees it as the call's result and the run goes on; with on_tool_exception="fail" (or ToolError::fatal) it fails the run.
A model-call, tool-call, token or nesting limit was reached; details.limit names it.
The structured output was still invalid after the allowed retries.
A hook returned an error.
The run state is not an agent's, or memory cannot find the run's namespace.
The input names one of the agent's own state keys, or tries to change the value that scopes the thread's memory.
An audit record could not be written, so the action it describes failed.
Another run holds the thread (OnBusy reject, or the wait timed out).
The thread waits for approval: answer it before sending more.
The thread's last run did not finish: continue it with retry.
The database could not be reached or timed out.
Another writer changed the thread first.
No checkpoint with that id.
Stored data could not be read.
The database was written by a newer schema version.
Encrypted data, or an encrypted database, without the key to read it.
A key does not match the one the database knows under its id.
The provider asked us to slow down.
The provider is overloaded.
The provider failed (5xx).
No answer in time: a model call, or (in a tool message) a tool call.
The connection failed or broke.
The provider refused the API key.
The key may not use this model or feature.
The provider does not know the model or endpoint.
The provider (or the gateway) rejected the request as malformed.
The conversation is longer than the model's context.
The provider's safety system refused the request.
Billing or quota is exhausted; another provider may still answer.
A successful response whose body could not be read (already billed, so not retried).
An unclassified provider failure.
The model's arguments did not match the tool's schema; the model sees the problems and may correct them.
The model called a tool the agent does not have.
The tool reported a failure meant for the model (ToolError).
An SDK agent configuration the engine could not build.
An SDK workflow that does not validate (`details.issues` lists the problems).
The feature needs a server, and here the engine runs as WebAssembly in a JavaScript host (the browser, design 0021): databases (SQLite, Postgres), encryption at rest, telemetry export, web tools.
An MCP server could not be started or reached, or refused the credentials (design 0022).
An MCP server answered something the client cannot use: a malformed message, an error, or a protocol version Criogen does not speak.
Two of an MCP server's tools map to the same name, or a name maps to nothing: set a prefix or leave one out with `except`.
An MCP tool's input schema is not an object schema, or is too large or too deep: leave the tool out with `except`.
An MCP server was not ready within the connect timeout.
The MCP server stopped (its process exited) or the client was closed.
The gateway needs a valid virtual key.
No route by that name, or the key may not use it.
The key's requests or tokens per minute are used up; Retry-After says when to try again.
Too many requests are in flight, over the gateway or for this key; Retry-After says when to retry.
The key's token budget is spent for the current day or month (Retry-After: until it ends), or in total.
